newsitem.title: POLAND: New Polish finmin says capital gains stay tax-free.
newsitem.headline: New Polish finmin says capital gains stay tax-free.

text.p: Poland's new Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday he will stick to the government's earlier agreed plan to keep capital gains tax-free for individual investors until the year 2000.
"It has been agreed that capital gains are to remain free of tax until the year 2000 and I do not see a reason for any changes," Belka told a news conference.

The extension of the tax exemption, originally due to expire on January 1, 1997, was proposed by Belka's predecessor Grzegorz Kolodko, who stepped down early this month, and passed by parliament in a tax package late last year.
Capital gains recorded by institutional investors are now compounded with other income and are subject to a flat 38-percent corporate income tax.
